nodes.text: Watch the hens — they've decided feet are a delicacy. What do you need?

choices.text: Spare an egg for the road?
How do you plan a farm year?

nodes.text: Next spring, the south strip goes to cotton. Jorel says the soil's wrong — the soil and I held a private meeting and the soil is *enthusiastic*. Tilo's loom sits hungry half the year and every bolt of cloth in this town walked here from somewhere else. Grow it, spin it, weave it, wear it — a whole trade, inside our own fence. Watch me.
Here — laid this morning, and the hen wants you to know it was her best work. {item:egg} Crack it over a pan at any campfire. An egg on the road is a small unfair advantage, and I believe in those.

In the seed ledger, in winter, by lamplight — every row, every rotation, three seasons deep. Jorel digs what I draw and swears the drawing's the easy half. He's right, but the ledger doesn't get blisters, so we've agreed not to compare.
Mind the gate latch — the cows have learnt Perl's and mine's likely next.
